service: VCF Automation provisioning service (Infrastructure as a Service API)

sourceOfTruth.statement: This contract is derived from reference documentation, not from a published API specification. VCF Automation (the successor to vRealize / Aria Automation) has no specification in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository (Apache-2.0), so every operation, path, parameter name, field name and field optionality recorded below was transcribed by hand from the Broadcom xAPIs reference pages enumerated in docs/official_sources.json. Where the reference pages are silent, this contract is silent: it is authoritative only for the five operations it names, and only for the details it states.
sourceOfTruth.referenceTitle: VMware Aria Automation Assembler IaaS API (VM Apps Org - Provisioning Service), version 9.1

fixtureNotice: Concrete values used by the loopback mock in this repository - API version strings, cloud account ids, host names, request tracker ids, passwords - are seed fixtures chosen for the exercise. They are not documented values. Only the operation set, paths, parameter names, field names and field optionality below come from the reference pages.

authentication.note: The reference pages mark the Authorization header as required on each operation. Obtaining the token is out of scope for this contract; no login operation is named here.

apiVersion.note: Documented as required on the PATCH operation and optional on the GET operations. GET /iaas/api/about documents no query parameters at all. The set of acceptable values is not documented; it is discovered at runtime from GET /iaas/api/about.

conventions.requestContentType: application/json for operations that carry a request body

deploymentId.description: ID of the deployment, this request is connected to

mockPolicy.purpose: Describes how the loopback mock in harness/MockAutomationServer.java behaves. It is a property of this repository's test double, not of the documented API.
mockPolicy.servedOperations: Only the five operations named above. Any other method or path is not served.
mockPolicy.errorMapping: The reference documents no status code for a malformed or unsupported request on these operations other than 403 and 404. The mock therefore answers a protocol violation with 404 ServiceErrorResponse for the GET operations and for unknown routes, and with 403 ServiceErrorResponse for the PATCH operation, always with an explanatory message field.
mockPolicy.determinism: All identifiers, timestamps and state transitions are fixed. Request tracker progress advances by poll count, never by wall-clock time.
mockPolicy.network: Binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port. No VMware endpoint is contacted at any point by the mock, the harness or the verifier.
